notes.title: NEW UPDATE 1.25 INTRODUCES JAPANESE, KOREAN AND CHINESE LANGUAGES INTO THE GAME!
notes.content:
Hello Horror fans,

[h3][b]We are adding 4 new languages to Song of Horror. Now, you can face The Presence and play the true horror in Korean, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, or Simplified Chinese![/b][/h3]

The new update opens the chance for more players over the globe to discover the hidden secrets of Song of Horror. We recognized there was a big group of Japanese, Korean and Chinese players supporting us, so we decided to work on integrating these languages into the game interface and subtitles, as part of our efforts to make it accessible to as many players as possible.

We hope that this new addition helps you investigate the scariest places and solve the most challenging puzzles. We also encourage you to keep sharing your best moments through the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1096570/discussions/]Steam forums[/url]... unless The Presence hunts you first.

Let the Horror begin,

[i]The Protocol Games & Raiser Games Teams.[/i]

notes.title: TO IMPROVE YOUR GAMING EXPERIENCE WE ARE REMOVING ASUS AURA COMPATIBILITY
notes.content:
Dear horror fans,

To improve your gaming experience while discovering the hidden secrets of this survival horror adventure, [b]we are removing Asus Aura support from Song of Horror[/b] since its integration was causing some issues that could prevent players from enjoying the game to the fullest.

However, as we are aware that some of you may want to still experience this feature on your computers, we will enable a dedicated branch with the Asus Aura version for you. You just need to follow the steps below to access this branch:
[olist]
[*] Go to your Steam Library
[*] Right Click on Song of Horror
[*] Select Properties
[*] Select Betas
[*] From the dropdown menu, select: "soh-v1.24_aura_enabled"
[*] As this is an open Beta there should not be any password prompt
[/olist]
Please note that when playing this branch with the Asus Aura activated (soh-v1.24_aura_enabled branch), you may encounter some bugs that even The Presence can't control, so we will no longer be providing support for these issues, and this branch. These are the bugs that you may encounter in the Asus Aura version:
[list]
[*] Fatal Error: some computers may receive a fatal error when launching the game, whether Aura is installed or not.
[*] Unable to advance to EP2: If you have EP2 purchased or Song of Horror Complete, you may not be able to advance to EP2, and the game will ask you to purchase this episode.
[/list]
[b]We strongly recommend you to play Song of Horror on the default branch[/b] to enjoy the best of experiences while playing the game.

[i]Fear The Presence.[/i]

[i]The Protocol & Raiser Games teams.[/i]

notes.title: Discover How Song of Horror Sneaks Under Your Skin
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

Fear is the rawest of feelings, wouldn't you agree? It's exciting, violent, intense... A mesmerizing emotion. You want to avoid it but, at the same time, you can't help but crave it, wanting to experience its sudden override of your senses over, and over again. Now, we are ready to unveil why.

This weekend, we are participating in a terrifying Livestream hosted during [url=https://www.paxegx.com/livestreams/egx-1/instigating-fear-in-horror-games]the EGX Digital event[/url]. We are joined by brilliant horror developers from [b]Supermassive Games[/b] (Until Dawn, Man of Medan) and [b]Red Ego Games[/b] (Re:Turn), as well as [b]the genre expert Louise Blain[/b], to share with you a unique look at fear. We will discuss the state of horror in 2020, how we crafted the unnerving atmosphere of Song of Horror, the methods that we use to create fear, and much more!

[h3]We are going live this Sunday, September 20th at 2:05 pm CET/8:05 am ET. Do not miss this special opportunity to understand true horror and go watch the stream [url=https://www.paxegx.com/livestreams/egx-1/instigating-fear-in-horror-games]right here[/url]![/h3]

We can't thank you enough for your support of Song of Horror. It is because of you that we can now talk about horror games with such outstanding guests, and to share this special moment with the greatest community.

Enjoy the show!

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams.

[i]"Four people arrive at the house, each with their own motives. Nothing but silence seems to inhabit the house... or is there something else lurking in the shadows?"[/i]

notes.title: Discover all the Secret References Hidding in Song of Horror - Episode 5!
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

Now that Episode 5 and thus Song of Horror is complete, we can finish [b]our series of steam events detailing all the references and easter eggs we have placed in Song of Horror[/b]! You can start [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1096570/announcements/detail/3439006723622979651]right here[/url] if you missed them.

[h3]Now, let's reveal the final secrets Song of Horror has in store for you![/h3]

[u][h3]EPISODE 5[/h3][/u]
• Dr. Berenice Prestegard, Ariadne's doctor, is named after [b]the short horror story from Edgar Allan Poe.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/8da42ede3657c7d02e04610a145dc808a6d4cc98.gif[/img]

• Jeremy Hartwood Mental Hospital, the place where Ariadne spent her childhood, shares its name with [b]the owner of Derceto Manor in the original Alone in the Dark[/b], whose suicide kick-starts the events of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/2a4fd95adcefc2530858137126175558e0663a5c.gif[/img]

• Alan Cedrac is a staff member of Jeremy Hartwood whose name comes from [b]Aline Cedrac, the co-protagonist of Alone in the Dark: A New Nightmare.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/41d429b56e48f6b2d19bbf0936ba915387fbcd0b.gif[/img]

• Edward Camby, the other co-protagonist of Alone in the Dark: A New Nightmare, also served as inspiration for another character from Song of Horror: [b]Edward Saunders, the director of Jeremy Hartwood.[/b] His surnames come from Grace Saunders, a child that acts as a supporting character in Alone in the Dark 2.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/ebea7f0e222adeb041234239927f44158bc232ca.gif[/img]

• In a document found inside Jeremy Hartwood, you can discover that the company that dismantled the hospital was Derceto (like the previously mentioned manor from Alone in the Dark) and [b]a reference to Ezechiel Pregzt, the antagonist of the same game.[/b]

[u][h3]ACHIEVEMENTS[/h3][/u]
[list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/0e77d9adfc3d93f1c6ab1e0f46d817e00355791f.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]The Masque of the Red Death (end of The First Dream)[/b]: Shares name with the homonymous story of Edgar Allan Poe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/fc3b7dc7281e6956ea4a5f08a168c04ad2a62947.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]The Oval Portrait (Find all Ariadne's drawings)[/b]: Another short story by Edgar Allan Poe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/bf9b8869cf2aa1620f58072ed6fb2626dc46c022.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]Morella (end of The Second Dream)[/b]: You guessed it, a third horror tale by Poe himself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/0ab2206bb422957c26640b4280587118ff0a3f4f.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]The Pit and the Pendulum[/b]: We recommend you check Edgar Allan Poe's work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/be592c2a95c8f10adf74c9f8e43fd5e58ebd322a.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]There and Back Again[/b]: The alternative title of "The Hobbit" from J.R.R. Tolkien.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/e8204f7535bc4705eda09e1058d5d8bd92c9372c.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]Alone in the Dark[/b] (complete Song of Horror with Daniel in Poe difficulty or superior): No explanation needed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/57eab8f05f5a77f1aad753887485649d60e89081.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]The Presence Waits Dreaming[/b] (beat the game on Lovecraft difficulty): A phrase from the short story "The Call of Cthulhu" by H.P. Lovecraft - "in his house at R'lyeh dead Cthulhu waits dreaming".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/4c6c7aa80dde1e7a935cdaa3fba35041fccda4b7.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]The Shadow Out of Time[/b]: Another reference to a short story by H.P. Lovecraft of the same name.
[/list]

[h3]How many of these references did you recognize? How many did you already find in Song of Horror? Let us know in the comments![/h3]

We hope you enjoyed this series of updates unveiling all the secrets we placed in Song of Horror. We are huge fans of the genre (obviously) and we believe you are as well (duh!), so we think you will appreciate these details as much as us!

[i]Thank you!

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams.

notes.title: New H.P. Lovecraft Difficulty Available Now! Introducing Update 1.22
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

[b]Today we introduce several, highly requested new features to Song of Horror![/b] You can now experience the hardest difficulty, H.P. Lovecraft, play as fan-favorite Erica in Episode 5, and face new scares and manifestations of The Presence.

We promised to add these three new elements to Song of Horror to keep improving the game beyond launch and to offer all of you new content to look forward to. This would not be possible without your participation in the community, so thank you for being so vocal and encouraging in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1096570/discussions/]the Steam forums[/url] and in your reviews!

[h3]Now, go and play the newest content Song of Horror has to offer![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/9508367be332303ff53adea90ddd6143362f127b.gif[/img]

[h3]Here's everything Update 1.22 introduces to Song of Horror:[/h3]

[h3][u]H.P. LOVECRAFT[/u][/h3]

[b]H.P. Lovecraft difficulty is now available![/b] H.P. Lovecraft is Song of Horror’s hardest difficulty level. You can unlock this new difficulty after beating the game for the first time in M.R. James or Edgar Allan Poe.
[list]
[*] The unlocking of H.P. Lovecraft is not retroactive: it won't unlock automatically if you already completed the game on M.R. James or Edgar Allan Poe. However, what you can do is watch the final cutscene again to unlock H.P. Lovecraft.
[*] H.P. Lovecraft is a global unlock. Once you obtain it, you’ll be able to select H.P. Lovecraft in any of your save slots.
[*] In H.P. Lovecraft, death (or worse!) lurks around every corner. The difficulty of all five Hauntings has been noticeably increased, and they will appear slightly more frequently than in Edgar Allan Poe. Lesser events will also tend to be more... malignant than before.
[*] Be on your guard! No tutorials will show up in H.P. Lovecraft (they are still accessible from the "Tutorials" section of the Pause menu), and you might find yourself facing dangers you didn’t expect.
[*] For those achievement hunters among us, you can now unlock a brand new one for completing the entire game on H.P. Lovecraft difficulty: [b]"The Presence waits dreaming".[/b]
[*] You can also change difficulty at any time between H.P. Lovecraft and the other three difficulty levels with no restrictions. However, doing this will prevent you from getting the achievement associated with H.P. Lovecraft, so think carefully before committing.
[/list]
[h3][u]EPISODE 5: NEW PLAYABLE CHARACTER AND EVENTS[/u][/h3]

[b]Erica Färber is now playable in Episode 5![/b] After going through unspeakable horrors at the Abbey of Saint Cecilia and the antique store, a final answer still eludes Erica, and as you know, she’s not one to sit idly by...
[list]
[*] To unlock Erica as a playable character in Episode 5, she needs to be present in Episode 4 and survive the ordeal (she doesn't need to be the one who finishes the episode). This is not retroactive: it will unlock on successful Episode 4 runs from now on.
[*] We also added [b]several instances of random paranormal activity[/b] to Jeremy Hartwood Mental Hospital. Now, your adventure through this cursed place will be scarier than ever before!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/6b6331181807e9701162e88dd74dcdea890c3d31.gif[/img]

[h3][u]THE ABYSS[/u][/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a rare bug where dodging an arm grab in the last second could result in your character still being grabbed and the associated icon not being properly shown.
[/list]
[h3][u]GENERAL[/u][/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed several translations and minor bugs.
[*] Fixed a bug where a certain combination of button/key presses could send you flying towards the last door you interacted with (The Presence can be really silly if it wants too).
[*] Fixed several minor sound issues.
[/list]

notes.title: We added a Game Mode Without Permadeath to Song of Horror!
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

We have listened to your opinions about permadeath and, following our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/ogg/1096570/announcements/detail/2189254554300963917]April's poll results[/url], we have added a new game mode to Song of Horror!

[h3]Introducing E.T.A. Hoffmann[/h3]
Named after the famous gothic author, E.T.A. Hoffmann is a new difficulty option where there is no permadeath. In this mode, [b]players can choose another character or re-start from the last checkpoint when a character dies.[/b] The Presence will also have the same difficulty level as MR James.

[h3]Now that we are closer than ever to the Final Episode, we feel it's the perfect moment to enjoy Episodes 1 through 4 in E.T.A. Hoffmann, to make sure your favorite characters reach the end![/h3]
[h3]About Permadeath in Song of Horror[/h3]
Song of Horror was designed to be a challenging, scary experience where permadeath is essential. We want you to feel the true fear and pressure of losing a character forever, that every action you take has a meaningful impact, that mistakes have real consequences... But also, that these consequences promote changing characters and experiencing Song of Horror from different perspectives.

However, we understand that every player is different. Some of you wanted to enjoy the story and gameplay of Song of Horror without permadeath getting in your way.

[h3]We recommend playing Song of Horror with permadeath for the first time... But, if the game was inaccessible to you due to this mechanic, we hope that the E.T.A Hoffmann difficulty will allow you to still enjoy it![/h3]
[i]Stay safe everyone!

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams.

[h3]There is nothing more marvelous or madder than real life.[/h3][/i]

notes.title: Discover all the Secret References Hidding in Song of Horror - Episode 1!
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

It is no secret that we are HUGE fans of survival horror games, but we are also fond of everything that pertains to horror in general: movies, TV shows, literature... That's why we placed so many references inside Song of Horror!

Many of you already noticed some of them, but there are still many easter eggs none of you have yet discovered. Now, we are ready to unveil all of them, starting with those hidden in the very beginning!

[h3]These are all the Easter Eggs you can find in the Prologue and Episode 1, [b]SPOILERS AHEAD[/b]:[/h3]

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/J5SJTcnC0LWFa9pAvr/source.gif[/img]

•    The sequence in which Daniel’s car is seen arriving at Husher's Mansion from a window is a nod to [b]one of the initial illustrations from Alone in the Dark[/b].

•    The sequence in which a playable character is introduced in front of the mansion is a nod to the [b]original Alone in the Dark cover[/b].

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/Q8IVJaF0H0nfLlaQDY/source.gif[/img]

•    The matchbox brand is a reference to [b]Project Zero/Fatal Frame[/b]. Specifically, to the camera film rolls that appear in the game.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/RiuQkkO5yIFmGSnBx3/source.gif[/img]

•    “Himuro” is the maker of the piano in Husher's residence, a nod to [b]the mansion in which Project Zero/Fatal Frame 1 takes place[/b].

•    There’s a poster in Julia’s room of a band called “Crimson”, which shows two red butterflies and several strings. This is a nod to [b]Project Zero /Fatal Frame II, “Crimson Butterfly”[/b].

•    The brand on one of the electrical fuses is called “Mafuyu”, a reference to [b]a character that goes missing in Project Zero /Fatal Frame[/b].

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/d6LHtqfsmBQ5qPeNyt/source.gif[/img]

•    The bird scare in Episode I is a reference to [b]an attack that players suffer in Alone in the Dark[/b], which has a similar camera point of view. (This happens in the hall on the first floor, heading towards the master bedroom from the hall on the right. It can be triggered the first or second time you walk by, or never at all. It’s more likely to happen as you exit the master bedroom.)

•    The face on the seal stamped on the letter from Färber to Husher belongs to [b]the famous horror writer M. R. James[/b].

•    “Abbot Thomas”, the street Husher lives on, is a reference to [b]a short story by M. R. James[/b].

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/VekCLkQCfISMpT1ZjH/source.gif[/img]

•    The YES/NO choice in the “sink” is a nod to all those wicked, impossible choices we are forced to make in horror games, decisions we should always say yes to (think “put your hand in the hole on the wall” in [b]Silent Hill 2[/b]).

•    The license plate on Daniel’s car reads “1994 ATD” ([b]1994 Alone in the Dark[/b]).

•    The logo of the security company that Alina works for is [b]the monolith from Dead Space[/b].

•    The publishing house that Etienne and Daniel work for is called [b]“Wake Publishing”[/b], in reference to Alan Wake.

•    The flashlight that every character carries (even though it’s IMPOSSIBLE to see) is made by a brand called [b]“Aline?”, the very question Edward poses each time he calls his partner on the radio in Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare[/b].

•    The lighter that every character carries has [b]the logo from Alone in the Dark[/b] (again, it’s practically impossible to see, unless you drop it and it falls right in front of the camera).

[h3]How many of these references did you know? How many did you already find in Song of Horror? Let us know in the comments! We have also placed several more in the last episode, so make sure to look out for those and share them with us![/h3]
[i]Stay strong.

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams.

[h3]Nothing but silence seems to inhabit the house... or is there something else lurking in the shadows?[/h3][/i]

notes.title: New Episode 5 Update: Lidia, Ariadne, The Presence, and much more!
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

[h3][b]Two weeks left before the launch of Episode 5!!![/b][/h3]
We are so close to the last verse of the song! Everything is coming to an end: The horrors you witnessed. The answers you needed. The characters that you lost, and those who survived. And The Presence, now fully unleashed, connecting them all.

Make sure to check [url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/1096570/view/2189254554278415610]our first update[/url] where we [b]show Jeremy Hartwood, share some details about the start of the story and more[/b]! And now, here's some new stuff you will find in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1158111/SONG_OF_HORROR_Episode_5/]Episode 5[/url]:

[h3]Playing with Lidia for the first time[/h3]
You all know Lidia since the beginning of Episode 2. She is a dear friend of Daniel, a committed social worker with a tragic past. During the 70s and the 80s, Lidia witnessed many friends and even love interests fall prey to heroin addiction. Since then, she assists people in poor neighborhoods, jails, conflict zones... Wherever she can.

Lidia met Daniel at her rehab program, where she guided him on his struggle against alcoholism. She became to his eyes a savior angel, and one of his best friends to date. Now, she is ready to commit the ultimate act of selflessness: [b]help Daniel get rid of the foreboding Song of Horror.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/2c5aa7fd842371ec0a515f2eb8de1609df5a9aa2.gif[/img]
[h3]Understanding the past to change the future[/h3]
In your terrifying adventure through Jeremy Hartwood mental hospital, you will find clues on the sinister events that took place there. One doctor in particular, Berenice Prestegard, seems to know more than anyone else. After all, she was the professional analyzing the mental state of Ariadne LeGrant-Amsberg when she was a child...

In certain moments of Episode 5, you will have the opportunity to [b]play as Dr. Prestegard in brief flashbacks from the 1920s[/b]. These scenes from the past will shed some light on the mysteries behind the LeGrant-Amsberg family, the song, and of course, The Presence. Will you be able to handle the truth?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/8da42ede3657c7d02e04610a145dc808a6d4cc98.gif[/img]
[h3]Ariadne, the central piece of the puzzle[/h3]
Through Berenice's flashbacks, you will meet Ariadne as a child. She hasn't changed much since then: driven mad by the effects of the song, everything she does and says doesn't seem to make any sense at all. Maybe this last trip will help you finally understand her, unraveling the warped thoughts trapped in the corners of her deranged mind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/88f4ce09dae2533da646062ac699b79b5f4ebd8d.gif[/img]
[h3]The Presence, unchained[/h3]
We have unleashed the Presence into Jeremy Hartwood! We are making sure that it behaves properly with our final tweaks, hunting you down through the creepy alleys of the hospital when you least expect it.

You are in its domains now: you can stay quiet, you can hide, you can run... But it will eventually catch up to you. Make sure to find everything you need to put on an end to its curse. This is your last chance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/23a83708113fdb2c2ba1d2ac09eb1f0e52b5f9b6.gif[/img]
[h3]The coda to the Song of Horror[/h3]
We have spent [b]the last six years of our lives[/b] creating Song of Horror, our unique take on survival horror. It hasn't been easy: developing the AI behind The Presence, designing the mechanics tied to the permadeath, and building the Song of Horror universe were steep challenges to overcome. We are proud to see how everything is coming along. But most importantly, we are so happy to see how you all are embracing this experience. The last moments of Song of Horror will leave you all speechless!

[i]Beware of The Presence!

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams

[h3]It's all over. Just a moment ago… I…[/h3][/i]

notes.title: Take a First-Look at Song of Horror Final Episode: The Horror and The Song!
notes.content:
Dear horror enthusiasts,

[b]We have finished the beta of Song of Horror Episode V: The Horror and the Song[/b]! We thought this would be a perfect moment to share with you new images and details of this last episode... So here we go!

[h2]The end is near[/h2]
Following the events of the previous episode, Daniel and his companions are now at a crossroads. He knows he is running out of time: the clock is ticking, faster than ever, closing the gap between his life and his death. His only hopes now rest in the information gathered in his most precious finding to date: [spoiler][b]Argos LeGrant's Diary[/b][/spoiler], where he finds a hidden note with a critical clue. Desperate, he truly feels this is his last opportunity to survive, and thus, he heads to Jeremy Hartwood Mental Hospital, in chase of the answer that will finally set him free from The Presence.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/tZRGghs.gif[/img]

[h2]Calling your friends, one last time[/h2]
In "The Horror and The Song", the character selection works differently. Looking at Daniel's phone contact agenda, [b]you can only choose one person to play this episode[/b]. If they die, it's Daniel's turn.

[h2]Exploring Jeremy Hartwood, the forgotten mental hospital[/h2]
Jeremy Hartwood Mental Hospital, once a recognized healthcare institution in the early XX Century, is now an abandoned building in the middle of nowhere. [b]This is the place where Ariadne spent her childhood[/b]. Just like Daniel, the staff of the hospital was trying to understand her odd behavior... Were they able to finish their research?

[img]https://i.imgur.com/JE8OR20.gif[/img]

Jeremy Hartwood is not only the last stage of Song of Horror, but also our take on the quintessential horror setting: the abandoned mental hospital. You will traverse the different wings of this oppressive facility to advance in Episode 5. We have even set a unique enigma where we push you to think about how certain elements can affect the building in different places (or as a whole).

[img]https://i.imgur.com/zxReLzv.gif[/img]

We are also focusing on the past in this episode: not only from the story perspective, but design-wise. Since you are in a XIX century Mental Hospital, you will find old documents and items that tell the story hidden within its walls. Some of them will expand your knowledge of the Song of Horror universe, while others will become the key to complete the story.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/fxI3HRs.gif[/img]
[h2]Next step: Integrating The Presence[/h2]

Now that Episode 5 is in place, we are focusing on the manifestations of The Presence in Jeremy Hartwood. The behavior of the AI behind the Song of Horror antagonist, as you know from your scary encounters, is unpredictable, and we have to make sure that The Presence does not escape from the boundaries of the hospital ;)

We are also adding the new characters and scenes, and working on the voice acting, general polish and high quality you can expect from this final episode. We will show you more about our latest progress in a future update, so stay tuned!

[i]Take care.

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams

[h3]"I need to sleep. I can only hope the nightmares won't be as horrible as real life."[/h3][/i]

notes.title: Song of Horror Episode 5, The Horror and The Song, Launches on May 28th
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

Recently, we have received several questions about [b]how the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic might affect Song of Horror’s development[/b].

Protocol Games is a Madrid (Spain)-based development studio. As you know, [b]both Spain and Madrid are being hit hard by COVID-19[/b], and we ourselves had to adjust our procedures to comply with current safety restrictions and regulations. We have set ourselves up to develop Song of Horror remotely as efficiently, considering the limitations of remote work.

Our decision to stay at home has proven to be beneficial since all four of us have been sick these past few weeks, with mild yet unpleasant symptoms coherent with a potential coronavirus infection. Despite this situation, [b]we are giving our all and doing our absolute best to guarantee the level of quality you have come to expect from us[/b].

However, there are certain aspects of development that escape our control. One of these cases is [b]the voice recording for Episode 5[/b]. The voice actors behind the characters of Song of Horror are currently staying at home as well, and the recording studio based in Paris is closed, following the recommendations of the healthcare system. We are looking for solutions to this and other occurrences with the help of our publisher, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/RaiserGames]Raiser Games[/url], who are also working remotely and helping us during this global situation.

[h3]Because of the previous set of events, we have made the hard decision of [b]launching the final episode of Song of Horror on May 28th.[/b] We believe this is necessary to deliver the perfect ending to the Song of Horror story.[/h3]

We will keep you informed on the development progress of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1158111/SONG_OF_HORROR_Episode_5/]Episode 5[/url] starting tomorrow, when we will share a first-look on the final episode of Song of Horror.

[i][b]Stay safe.

The Protocol Games team[/b][/i]

notes.title: The Community Has Spoken: Are We Adding the New Game Mode Without Permadeath?
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

Song of Horror was designed to be a challenging, scary experience where permadeath is essential. We want you to feel the true fear and pressure of losing a character forever, that every action you take has a meaningful impact, that mistakes have real consequences... But also, that these consequences promote changing characters and experiencing Song of Horror from different perspectives.

However, we understand that every player is different. Some of you wanted to enjoy the story and gameplay of Song of Horror without permadeath getting in your way.

Now, thanks to your participation in our latest poll, we already know your final answer: [b]you want Song of Horror to have a game mode without permadeath and keeping the same aggressiveness level of The Presence.[/b] You can check all the results of the survey right here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/8bdb883917397a078a0721514f3f9f2b23c30236.jpg[/img]

This new game mode will be called [b]E.T.A. Hoffmann, where players can choose another character or re-start from the last checkpoint when a character dies[/b]. The Presence will also have the same difficulty level as MR James. We will launch the E.T.A. Hoffmann difficulty option alongside Episode 5, so look forward to that![/b] 

[h3]We recommend playing Song of Horror with permadeath for the first time... But, if the game was inaccessible to you due to this mechanic, we hope that the E.T.A Hoffmann difficulty will allow you to still enjoy it![/h3]

[i]Stay safe everyone!

The Protocol & Raiser Games Teams.[/i]

[h3][i]That place, that melody... God... I'm running out of time.[/i][/h3]

Because of the previous reason, we are considering adding a new difficulty option called [b]E.T.A. Hoffmann[/b], where [b]players can choose another character or re-start from the last checkpoint when a character dies[/b].

notes.title: Song of Horror's Biggest Update: Here's Everything We Are Adding to Episode 4
notes.content:
Dear Song of Horror fans,

We are introducing our biggest update to date right now! This patch features [b]important changes to Episode 4[/b], bringing it closer to the experience we originally wanted to create. As such, you can expect new features and improvements destined to craft a scarier, and tenser atmosphere throughout the whole episode (which means you are going to have a really bad time!).

Here's the new content we are adding to Episode 4 (and a couple of tweaks in Episode 3!):

[h2]UPDATE 1.14[/h2]
[h3]EPISODE 4[/h3][list]
[*] [b]25 new paranormal events[/b]: St. Cecilia's Abbey is officially the most haunted place in Song of Horror. You can expect more scares than ever before!
[*] An original collectible: [b]The Tarot Deck[/b]. Find five fate-altering confessions from those consumed by The Presence to resist its most lethal attacks.
[*] [b]New cutscenes[/b] + animation fixes: We introduced more cinematic moments and tweaked several animations from characters during said scenes.
[*] [b]A new illustrated cutscene[/b] at the end of the episode, adding more context and emotion before the last episode.
[*] The "Ornate keys" now combine into a single item upon having more than one of them.

[*] The Scriptorium blocked door can now be opened from the inside, more exploration possibilities!

notes.title: Don't miss this exclusive interview where we talk about The Presence!
notes.content:
Greetings, horror fans!

It's been a few days since we put ourselves in this fearsome adventure where the Presence is always watching you and playing by its own rules. That's it, this dark entity responds to the player's action, creating many different situations, even if you do exactly the same...

To discover more, we bring you an [url=https://www.xataka.com/videojuegos/song-of-horror-videojuego-espanol-terror-que-inteligencia-artificial-aprende-ti-para-matarte-asustarte-siempre]exclusive interview from Xataka[/url], (originally in Spanish) where we talk about the process of creating The Presence, "the damn thing that still manages to scare them".

Let the horrors begin...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/2e1d145d6d8d084cd6a9c5e4e85ad29923ea5efe.jpg[/img]

There are many theories that attempt to explain why so many people enjoy [b]scary films and video games[/b]. One of the most common brought up by psychologists is 'emotional regulation', a term that describes experiencing an emotion in a controlled setting. When you watch a horror film, you’re expecting scares – you’re ready for them and give in to your reactions. You might scream, cover your eyes, or even jump, but you know everything will be just fine because you're sitting in your living room and you know everything will go back to normal once it’s over.

We also like horror for the same reason that we keep going back to the same pizza place: whenever we go there, we have a good time. Audio-visual genres (comedy, drama, science fiction, etc.) have a [b]degree of predictability[/b] and, therefore, of expectation. "Whenever I watch horror movies, I enjoy them", we think to ourselves. And so we watch horror movies.

Now, a Spanish team has developed a video game to put horror fans’ wits to the test, because everything that happens during gameplay is completely unpredictable. Literally. Not even the developers themselves know exactly what might happen. According to the developers, it’s all thanks to an [b]Artificial intelligence[/b] that makes sure it’s [b]impossible to predict the scares[/b].

[h1]The (evil) Presence[/h1]
[b]'Song of Horror'[/b] is an adventure in psychological terror that takes its cues from legendary titles such as [b]'Alone in the Dark'[/b] and [b]'Resident Evil'[/b]. Everything kicks off with the disappearance of a famous writer ¬– and it’s your job to find him. The search will take players into his home, where it becomes clear that something sinister is hiding within its four walls.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/9411bc79089e2e1b9d7ebcf674c6f4f1ff03eb94.jpg[/img]
[i]From left to right: David Navarro, Ignacio Fernández and Carlos Grupeli, the creators of 'Song of Horror'[/i]

The game's creators, led by [b]Ignacio Fernández[/b], [b]Carlos Grupeli[/b] and [b]David Navarro[/b], (who we spoke to for this article) decided to call this sinister something 'The Presence', and tasked it with making your time with the game as unsettling as possible. In the words of Ignacio:

[h1][i]'What I see in 'Song of Horror' that I don't see in other horror games nowadays is the threatening, tense atmosphere that was palpable in the first 'Alone in the Dark'.  That feeling of 'this is so scary, if I blow it now I'll have to start all over'. The fear is a bit more mature, more of a constant pressure on you."[/i] [/h1]

One of the ways this is achieved is through permadeath (i.e. if one of the 13 playable characters dies, they are dead forever) and The Presence, which in effect acts as the 'monster' that, according to the experts, all works of horror should feature. Such [b]monsters [/b]are often used either so that we can empathize with them and unleash our wild side by siding with the enemy of our beloved characters, or simply out of curiosity to learn more about them (in fact, the philosopher Noël Carroll believes that the process of discovering the monster, of getting to know it and its motives, etc, is another reason why we're hooked on horror as a genre).

Not to contradict any of these experts or philosophers, but the truth is that The Presence doesn't make itself easy to empathize with, especially given that not even its own 'parents' know what it's going to do next.

[h1]An AI that plays by its own rules.[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/f790202a2eef3411377fdcdbf07fa8bef7bc238a.jpg[/img]
[h1][i]"The Presence watches the player. As the player enters The Presence's territory, it responds to the intrusion and continues to respond in answer to the player's actions: how far they intrude, how quickly, and so on. We always kept the famous 'dog scare' from 'Resident Evil' in mind. The first time you're terrified, the second time, well, you still get a fright, but by the third, you barely react. With The Presence it's different. Even if you do exactly the same thing, it will respond differently. You have no control over it because it plays by its own rules".[/i][/h1]

It was Carlos who defined The Presence this way. He was the main person in charge of programming the artificial intelligence that brings the monster to life. He explained to us that over the five years it has taken to develop the game, they have input ever more [b]variables, weapons, and tools[/b] for the Presence. He spoke of the [b]many factors that 'it' takes into account before making a move[/b]: if you attempt to open a door X number of times, if you try X number of light switches, if you spend X number of seconds in a room, if you move quickly or slowly, etc.

[u][b]The Presence watches you, and every movement you make or thing you do provokes a reaction (or not)[/b][/u]

Ignacio notes that, with The Presence, even when a floorboard squeaks as you step in a certain place, it's different from it not squeaking. And with so much granularity and so many variables, our next question was obvious: how did you program something like that? "We're talking about small elements here which, when combined, give rise to a universe of possibilities, basically in an intrinsic way, without us having to force anything", says Carlos. In other words, they basically input a massive number of variables.

To complicate matters even more, [b]each playable character has certain traits[/b] which bring their own set of variables to the game. A stealthy character isn't the same as a strong one, and all those circumstances come together to affect the difficulty of the game. For example, if The Presence attacks you by suddenly opening a door, it will be more difficult for you to block it if your character is weaker – but that might just be the character you need to solve a particular puzzle. "Depending on what you're good at, you will have to sacrifice certain traits", Ignacio explains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/fb68eee7a73f8dae772de7d53992266b37e757d4.jpg[/img]

And as if that isn’t enough, [b]The Presence goes even further[/b]. It's not the same in the first chapter as it is in the fifth and final chapter of the game. "In each chapter, we've added new elements – some specific to that chapter, and others to The Presence itself. As you enter its territory and learn more about its history, it becomes more aggressive and visually more powerful. From glimpsing a pair of hands to shrouding everything in darkness, the level of visual intensity increases. It becomes more and more apparent", Ignacio notes.
 
What's it like to design levels that feature so much uncertainty? The developers admit that there are 'unique events' that happen to everyone, no matter what. Ignacio elaborates:

[i][h1]"Sometimes we have to tether The Presence to force certain things to happen during the game. For example, let's say that in one chapter we want the same event to happen in a specific place to all players. Obviously, the game contains the same puzzles, scenes and so on for everyone. What changes is the gameplay. There’s an event in chapter one where we don’t want anything else to happen, so we have to stop The Presence for a bit and release it later. It's a little more tricky".[/h1][/i]

The same goes for the [b]setting and music[/b]: "Each room has a mood, its own background music. But later when The Presence gets involved, it has its own music. When it makes a major appearance, its theme begins and all the others stop. What's more, it usually begins with a bang", Ignacio explains.

For everything else, however, the developers assure us that [b]The Presence makes its own decisions in response to the stimuli it receives[/b] at any given time. "Most of the tools The Presence has in its arsenal can be used if not everywhere, then almost everywhere", Ignacio concludes.

[h1][i]"The fun part of testing this game, even though I've played it about 400 times, is that sometimes even now the damn thing still manages to scare us"[/i][/h1]

According to Carlos, "The fun part of testing this game, even though I've played it about 400 times, is that sometimes even now the damn thing still manages to scare us". To which Ignacio adds, "Not long ago we thought there was a bug because The Presence did a combination of things we hadn't seen before. We checked and it turned out everything was fine, but we had to go over the code with a fine-tooth comb. But these combinations of things unsettle you, they surprise you".
 
[h1]Five years to learn how to make a video game from scratch[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/77a709993ff5413a00144343fee20d66a7de9f9c.jpg[/img]
[i]Carlos and Ignacio during one of the first-ever public presentations of 'Song of Horror' at a video games event (2015).[/i]

The interesting thing about the boys from Protocol, the developers of 'Song of Horror, is that Ignacio is an architect, Carlos is a computer technician, and David studied Fine Arts. [b]None of them had any prior experience in the world of video games[/b]. There was nothing else for it but to start from scratch.

"The first year we were just taking everything in", Ignacio recalls. "We watched people playing and took note of anything strange that happened, or parts that were too boring. We've since polished all that up and, in fact, joke amongst ourselves that we're actually on 'Song of Horror' 2 or 3 thanks to all of the improvements we've made along the way. The second year was the polishing stage, and the other 3 have been about making the game we truly saw in our imaginations", he finishes.

[h1][i]"We've had lots of support, especially with the financial side of things. Our families have made so many sacrifices"[/i][/h1]

The trio confessed that they did the bulk of the work on the game with Luis, another programmer, and that in total some 15 people worked on developing the game (including collaborators for some specific matters). Meanwhile,[b] they themselves supplied all of the funding[/b] (they had two failed rounds on Kickstarter) which, as they explain it, led to some very difficult moments. "Over and above my own and Ignacio's personal savings, the rest of the time we have been lucky that our close family and friends have been able to support us. We've received a lot of support, especially financially. Our families have made many sacrifices for us", Carlos admits.

It's only logical then that they will have encountered problems within the video games industry. "In many areas, I don't think we're taken seriously in the way that cinema is, for example", says David, to which Ignacio adds, "The problem is that ultimately it's a global market, and we're competing with studios that have much larger teams and better funding".
In any event, it's admirable that they've managed to develop such a complex game from scratch and get it off the ground, centered around such an interesting AI concept. As Ignacio himself proudly states, "In monetary terms, we're not an AAA, but when it comes to things that don't depend solely on money, such as the details or the narrative, I believe we measure up just fine".

notes.title: Song of Horror Episode 3 launches on December, Friday 13th!
notes.content:
Greetings, horror fans,

We are launching Song of Horror newest episode on December, Friday 13th!

Following the trail of evidence, the third episode sees play moves to the State University of Arts and Humanities - both Husher’s place of work, and mysteriously the last place he was seen alive. You will find yourself joining forces with some of Husher’s closest acquaintances, bringing in new threads of plot as The Presence ups its attacks and the truth looms large.

[h1]In Song of Horror - Episode 3, you will:[/h1][list]
[*] Continue the adventure in a [b]haunted university[/b], cursed by the Song of Horror.
[*] [b]Change characters[/b] throughout the episode on some particular points to explore and progress through different areas of the university.
[*] Encounter [b]new characters[/b] who join the story: Omar Nassiri, Husher’s coworker, and Grace Richards, Husher’s pupil, as well as an appearance from a surprising character.
[*] Take on even more [b]unique events[/b], threats, and challenges by The Presence.
[/list]

[h1]You can visit Song of Horror's Episode 3 page [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1157230/SONG_OF_HORROR_Episode_3/]here[/url].[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/ae840548b6aeba49552ecd0e8579adca570c1348.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/09268cf35ca2698ad954ad4e0bcaa3e59ae057ca.jpg[/img]

Remember that there are several options to play Song of Horror, but the one we recommend is the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/11895/SONG_OF_HORROR_Founder_Limited_Edition/]Founder Limited Edition[/url] at the special price of $19.99/€19.99/£17.14, which is [b]only available until the end of 2019[/b]! With this edition, you can get all Song of Horror's Episodes. Alternatively, you can pick each episode of Song of Horror individually on Steam for $7.99/€7.99/£6.99, or as part of the Season Pass that will unlock a further two episodes on top of the existing three in the months ahead for $21.99/€21.99/£18.99.

All five episodes each pay homage to a specific [b]survival horror genre classic[/b]. The debut episode - which sees your encounter against The Presence for the first time - tips its hat to Infogrames’ classic series [b]Alone in the Dark[/b], while episode two is especially pleasing if you are a fan of the phenomenal [b]Silent Hill[/b]. The brand news third episode, however, owes most to survival horror classic [b]Obscure[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/9063e57d0bd45d23a3c2a8a35d21105f2d31878a.jpg[/img]

We are so happy with the reception of the game that [b]we wanted to share with you some of our favorite comments from the community[/b]:

[i]"This is honestly one of the best horror games in this decade!!!"

"After playing 2 released episodes this becomes my fav horror game in the recent decade."

"Great game, I made a good purchase, congratulations"

"This game is actually somewhat unique"

"Finding this game is like finding my soul mate"

"Song of Horror is AMAZING! I’ve played so many terrifying horror games and that game was the first to have me on edge for the entire playthrough!"

"I love you devs, best horror game of the year"

"You all seem so passionate about making the game that it makes me want it even more!! It looks amazing!"

"I had an amazing stream playing Song of Horror. Such a good game so far. I am really enjoying it."

"Bought it yesterday and the last two horror games I've bought on steam I've returned but not this one. Love it..."[/i]

Thank you everyone for the kind words! We are eager to share with you more about Song of Horror's Episode 3 and look at your reactions!

[i]Beware of The Presence!!![/i]

notes.title: Song of Horror's first ever update is HERE! The Horror Continues...
notes.content:
Dear horror fans,

We had a wonderful launch day on Halloween, playing live with all of you and enjoying the scariest night of the year together. We are so happy to read all your positive comments about Song of Horror! The reception of the game has been great overall, and we want to thank all of you for your support, love, and feedback...

...That's why we are able to introduce today [b]the first official update of Song of Horror[/b]! We've focused on improving and fixing several aspects of the game attending to your requests and petitions. You can take a look at everything we are adding to Song of Horror, including quality-of-life improvements, gameplay tweaks, audiovisual changes, and bug fixing:

[h1]THE PRESENCE[/h1][list]
[*] Fixed rare instance of lost characters appearing when they shouldn’t.
[*] Detecting danger when listening at doors should now be easier.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/cd366872dc4281e6a8761341d554b24cd680aac4.jpg[/img]

[h1]THE SILENCE[/h1][list]
[*] Characters now utter a voice phrase on overcoming The Silence.
[*] Added missing startled character sounds when The Silence begins.
[*] Fixed several instances of The Silence happening where it shouldn’t, causing bizarre camera bugs & possible blocks.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/e853935256775a0d7a0e9f6f696bd6b617062686.jpg[/img]

[h1]THE DARKNESS[/h1][list]
[*] Heartbeat sound has been adjusted for clarity.
[*] Increased heartbeats’ successful timing range, with an even greater increase in M.R. James difficulty.
[*] Slightly increased the average time between shrieks.
[*] Politely asked The Presence to stop generating Darkness events in some very specific places where your way to a hiding spot would be blocked.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35590000/d728bea75c06c85fcb6a78e21fa197de9c0cebf6.jpg[/img]

[h1]EPISODE 1[/h1][list]
[*] Fixed some wrong texts belonging to Alina.
[*] Changed the sound you hear when listening to Saul’s room door to be more sinister and indicative of danger.
[/list]

[h1]EPISODE 2[/h1][list]
[*] Fixed some wrong texts belonging to Alexander.
[*] Fixed a wrong clue in the keys puzzle document.
[*] Fixed a loading bug that could happen on saving and quitting while standing on stairs, by which you’d be stuck in the wrong camera on loading, without your character in sight.
[*] Fixed several map icons related to Etienne’s note folder and several wrongly placed standard map icons.
[*] Fixed the character arm movement when using a Coltar token in the Coltar machine.
[*] Fixed a bug with Coltar messages’ texture.
[*] Fixed an instance of characters using voice lines from a different character than them.
[*] You no longer should lose all remaining characters when losing a character in the infinite hallway.
[*] Subtitles for “Recording 3 by Isaac Färber” should now be properly in sync with the audio.
[*] Fixed a few visual and audio bugs in the ending cinematic sequences.
[*] Added subtitle to Rene’s gun cocking for players with “Visual Cues” option enabled.
[/list]

[h1]GENERAL[/h1][list]
[*] Slightly tweaked speaking facial animations.
[*] Translated some texts which had been left in Spanish.
[*] Modified Resolution selector text to clarify it only affects resolution in Windowed mode. In Fullscreen mode, it should detect your screen’s native resolution if it’s 16:9, and the closest one if it isn’t.
[*] Added 1440p (2560x1440) resolution to Windowed Mode Resolution selector.
[/list]

Remember that more episodes are on their way. We cannot wait to share with all of you what we have in store for the next months, stay tuned!

[i]Beware of The Presence...[/i]

notes.title: JOIN US ON OUR SONG OF HORROR LAUNCH LIVE STREAM IN HALLOWEEN!
notes.content:
Hello, horror fans!

We are getting really close to the launch of Song of Horror, the game we have been developing during the last five years of our lives. We want to celebrate this anticipated date with all of you, and that's why we are going to [b]stream Song of Horror live on Halloween[/b]!

We invite all of you to join us during the launch of Song of Horror, starting at [b]4 pm CET/11 am EST[/b], here on Steam. We'll be doing four simultaneous streamings with the four different playable characters of the first episode, sharing development stories, quirky anecdotes, cool references... And of course, getting scared live! Even after playing the game for more than 400 times, we still get chills when playing it.

[previewyoutube=20xHEYb2_Es;full][/previewyoutube]

A professional makeup artist will be here as well to help us dress for Halloween. Don't miss the chance to watch all of us dress up as iconic Halloween characters (and maybe some of our own as well!). We invite you to do the same and share with us your freaky Halloween costumes and Song of Horror gameplays on social media with the hashtag [b]#SongOfHorrorLivestream[/b].

[h1]This will be the most memorable Halloween of our lives. We want to share this exciting experience with all of you.[/h1]

[i]Do not forget, The Presence will always be watching you...[/i]
